what_you_saw_in_the_pictures: Icons light and dark: the 9 stroke icons are crisp and theme correctly (dark on white, light on dark). The first captures of the Icons and Button section frames showed a flat grey frame with invisible titles: a stale placeholder colour left after a rerun. I fixed it in the generator (the paint helper now stores the resolved colour), ran 00 and 06, captured again, and both are now correct.

Button light and dark: 114 variants in a grid. The focus ring sits 2 px outside each button. Disabled shares one grey look. Loading shows the spinner. The iconOnly buttons are square. No clipped text. In dark, the neutral button becomes white, and the dangerSoft label is red on deep red (readable).

Input light and dark: 21 variants. The placeholder is lighter than the value. Hover darkens the border. Focus ring, invalid red 2 px border with error icon and message, disabled and readOnly fills are all visible. Text wraps without clipping.

Tabs light and dark: line triggers with a brand underline when selected and pill triggers with a filled selected state, focus rings visible. In the vertical example the indicator sits on the bottom edge rather than the start edge, which is wrong.

DropdownMenu light and dark: highlighted rows are inverted (neutral fill, inverse text), and the danger row is red. Checked rows show a check or dot. The model-selector content has a border and corners. All readable.

Dialog light: two sizes and the overlay example. The shadows of the set are clipped at the set bounds. Dialog dark: the dialog fill equals the section background and its border is transparent, so in the set it has almost no visible edge. It reads fine on the overlay.

Desktop assistant light and dark: top bar with Tabs (Chat selected), a user bubble and an assistant message, a composer with Input and a primary arrow-up button, and the open model menu anchored above the 'Standard ^' trigger. No overlap except the menu covering the input, which is intended. The composer shows two nested borders.

Mobile Delete project light and dark: a dimmed settings page with two filled Inputs and Export (secondary) and Delete project (danger) buttons, all visible above the dialog. The dialog sits at the bottom with a secondary Cancel and a danger Delete project. In the first version the dialog was centred and covered the buttons, so I moved it to the bottom in the generator and rebuilt the screen.

Icon stroke weight is a raw 2 at every size (it is part of the icon's geometry); at 16 px the icons look heavy.

Layout values from the template, not the spec, are raw: positions, the focus-ring offset placement, the tab indicator's 2 px height, fixed showcase widths (Input 320, item 200, content 240, dialog at its max width), section padding and gaps. The tab indicator's thickness is bound to width/md, which comes from the extensions stylesheet, not the spec.
The first 01a run failed (the runtime renamed every variant to 'root'). Figma rolled the call back and nothing was left; the generator was fixed and the script rerun.

results.what: I finished the four token-tool changes on branch v2-direction. 1) build-tokens.mjs now gives every semantic and proposed token a description. Figma's own text wins when it has one; otherwise the text comes from ds-tokens/descriptions.json. Each description goes into the DTCG files as $description and into tokens.json as "description" plus a new "descriptionSource" field. The build fails if a token has a description in neither place. 2) diff-figma.mjs now treats a Motion duration held as a number in Figma (100) and the same number in ms in the repo ("100ms") as equal, so the sandbox diff shows 0 drift. figma-patch-list.md has a third section, "Descriptions to set", grouped by collection. The proposed-token list now says the snapshot reads variables only, so a shadow Figma keeps as an effect style is still listed. 3) lint-tokens.mjs has the four refinements (scopes, missing categories, the four unlisted collections, and the state-segment message). Every change has its own planted case. All commands ran. The three self-tests exit 0. ds-tokens/audit was backed up before the sandbox runs and restored afterwards, and `diff -r` confirmed the restore. The sandbox results are saved in v2/figma/sandbox/results/. build-report.mjs ran last.
added_or_changed: v2/tools/build-tokens.mjs: build() takes a 4th argument (descriptions). Figma's description wins; otherwise the one from descriptions.json. The source is the first word of the entry's source field and must be one of figma, owner, proposed or drafted. A token with no description fails under code 'description'. Bad, empty or duplicate entries also fail. Descriptions are written as $description in the semantic DTCG files, and descriptionSource is added to their $extensions. tokens.json gets 'descriptionSource' right after 'description'; no other field changed (checked against the earlier file: 331 tokens, 0 other field differences). The run prints a count of descriptions by source. Files are now written whole to a temporary file and renamed into place. The build stops if descriptions.json is missing. 7 new planted cases; the self-test now has 17.

v2/tools/diff-figma.mjs: new 'duration' kind for Figma Motion numbers and code type 'duration'. It reads N, 'N', 'Nms', 'Ns' and {value, unit}. The plain 'number' kind still treats 100 and '100ms' as different. List 8 items now carry repoSource. patchList() has a third section, 'Descriptions to set': one row per Figma variable with an empty description and a description in the repo, grouped by collection in Figma's order, with columns Name, Description to paste and Source. A Figma description that differs from the repo's is not listed there. List 9's label and the 'Variables to add' introduction explain that a token Figma keeps as a style is still listed. diff.json inputs.figma now names the snapshot folder actually read. Self-test: the expected patch list is updated to three sections; added a description grouping case (Themes then Radius, plus a differing Figma description that is not listed); added a Motion case (sameValue checks, plus an end-to-end fixture where 100 = '100ms' agrees and 160 against '170ms' is the only drift).

v2/tools/lint-tokens.mjs: (a) scopes: a primitive with empty scopes is no longer a finding. A primitive with ALL_SCOPES is a 'decide' finding with the requested wording. A semantic token with empty scopes is still 'breaks the standard', except in Motion, where it is a 'note'. (b) missing-categories: a category is also covered by a non-empty collection of that purpose: Border with width/*, Size, Motion, or an Elevation collection. Effect styles are read from <snapshot folder>/styles.txt when that file exists. With no styles.txt, elevation is reported as 'Cannot tell from the snapshot'. The focus-ring pattern also accepts focus/width and ring/width-style names. (c) Border, Size, Motion and Elevation now appear in one 'decide' finding with the requested wording, and are no longer repeated as empty or as off the category list. (d) the state-segment message now names the fix: 'rename so the state word is not a group name, for example ring/width instead of focus/width'. lint.json sources now name the snapshot folder read. Self-test: 5 new cases, each testing one rule in isolation, and the exit condition now requires every case to pass.

problems: The sandbox snapshot stores Border width/md's description with the HTML entity ' where the repo has an apostrophe, so the sandbox diff lists 1 description difference. Because Figma's description wins in the build, a build from a snapshot like that would carry the entity into tokens.json and the DTCG files. This is a fault in how Figma was exported or written, not in the tools.
Elevation shows as 'cannot tell from the snapshot' on both snapshots. No styles.txt exists in v2/figma/ or v2/figma/sandbox/, and creating one was not on my edit list.
